title: Interview coda — Juniper Kline
content:
Brain-dump (late evening) — trying to capture impressions, concrete evidence, and a minimal recommendation for a fast handoff. Not polished, intentionally fragmentary.

Quick summary:
- Candidate: Juniper Kline — applied for Senior Runtime Engineer (inference engine). Strong low-level intuition about memory/KV cache tradeoffs, thoughtful about quantization implications for model accuracy. Polished communicator but occasionally over-indexed on single-solution heuristics.

What stood out (evidence):
- KV cache mental model: sketched a good diagram on call that matched our runtime assumptions (segmented caches, eviction heuristics tied to token-age + token-frequency). Mentioned multi-tenant cache isolation and described a cheap async scrubber approach — plausible and pragmatic.
- Quantization discussion: comfortable with 4-bit flows and aware of per-layer sensitivity; brought up per-layer calibration, and proposed a fallback path for sensitive heads. Showed concrete experiment design to detect quality regressions (calibration set + KL divergence threshold). Good sign.
- Batching/latency tradeoffs: recommended a dynamic batching policy based on short-tail latency SLOs; suggested an estimator that uses recent prefix distributions to set batch window. Conceptually sound, but didn't fully account for pathological workloads (bursty API customers).
- System design: on the whiteboard, drew an autoscaling sketch for a dedicated pool with heterogeneous GPU types. Reasonable, but glossed over orchestration complexity (state migration during scale-down).
- Coding taste: take-home exercise looked tidy; used clear tests, small helpers, but had one edge-case bug in stream cancellation path. Fix is trivial.

Risks / open concerns:
- Tendency to latch: when probing on failure modes, Juniper latched onto the cache scrubber idea and spent long time defending it rather than enumerating alternatives. Could be sign of lower epistemic humility in debates with senior peers.
- Operational experience: good on theory, less evidence of having owned infra facing dozens of high-qps customers with live rollouts. Asked about postmortems and incident triage but answers were more process-oriented than concrete (i.e., 'we have runbooks' vs. 'here's what I'd tweak in practice').
- Leveling ambiguity: feels Senior IC, possibly borderline Staff depending on how much ownership and cross-team influence we expect immediately.

Suggested on-site / final loop focus areas:
- Live debugging session: give a synthetic load that triggers cache thrash and ask candidate to debug telemetry and propose mitigations on the spot. This will reveal operational instincts.
- Ownership scenario: run a 20-minute role-play where candidate must design a rollout from canary to full for a quantized model variant, including metrics to watch and automated rollback criteria.
- Pair-program: stream cancellation path fix + add a regression test that simulates partial consumer disconnects. Confirm they can iterate on tests quickly.

Provisional score (my gut):
- Technical signal: 7/10 (strong design + experiments, misses in ops depth)
- Team fit/communication: 8/10 (clear, calm in docs and verbal, collaborative tone)
- Hiring recommendation: green with conditions — hire at Senior, with an expectation ramp that includes shadowing SRE/ops for first 8–12 weeks and a concrete onboarding assignment to own a rollout.

Suggested leveling blurb for hiring packet:
- "Juniper Kline — Senior Runtime Engineer. Demonstrates strong systems thinking around KV caching and quantization; proposes measurable experiments and fallback strategies. Recommend hire at Senior IC. Suggested initial goals: (1) deliver a safe per-layer quantization rollout prototype with telemetry hooks; (2) pair with SRE on a live cache thrash postmortem and create improved runbook items."

Notes to self / next steps:
- Share this draft with Aria and Miles for quick sanity check before posting to hiring doc.
- If we push to on-site, craft the live-debug harness (simulate 10% of requests with long prefixes to induce cache churn).
- Pick 3 short calibration prompts for the quantization experiment so we have a reproducible quality baseline.

Unresolved questions I want answered before final packet:
- Has Juniper shipped cross-region fallback logic in prod (they said yes but gave high-level answer)? Need an example PR / postmortem.
- Who owns the cache eviction policy where they last worked? Was it a single repo or a multi-service contract? Impacts onboarding friction.

Random personal notes (raw):
- Liked their metaphor: 'cache is a thermostat not a bank' — simple and probably useful for onboarding docs.
- They reacted well to pushback on rollout speed; adjustable risk profile seemed realistic.
- Could be an excellent mentor for mid-level folks on principled experiment design.

End of dump. Will tidy up after quick sync with Aria.
